## The same decomposition works in 2D and 3D {#iv7-dimensions .vector-lesson .projection-lesson }

```{=html}
<p>Choose a non-zero direction <span data-math="\underset{\sim}{b}"></span>.</p><div class="pr-eq"><span data-math="\displaystyle \underset{\sim}{a}=\underbrace{\frac{\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{b}}{|\underset{\sim}{b}|^2}\underset{\sim}{b}}_{\text{parallel component}}+\underbrace{\left(\underset{\sim}{a}-\frac{\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{b}}{|\underset{\sim}{b}|^2}\underset{\sim}{b}\right)}_{\text{perpendicular component}}"></span></div><p>Use two components or three when calculating the scalar product and magnitude.</p><div class="pr-takeaway"><p>Breaking a vector into these two parts is a skill we will use in many application problems.</p></div>
```
